bullets.title: NVDA pre-earnings: 7 down days, Vera Rubin 30x efficiency leap, SpaceX partnership
bullets.body: NVDA is set for a 7th consecutive down day ahead of Wednesday earnings, with Goldman's One-Delta desk flagging it as 'top of mind.' On the positive side, NVIDIA's Vera Rubin delivers on-silicon benchmarks of 30x throughput/MW and 35x lower token cost vs. GB300 for agentic AI, and Elon Musk announced SpaceX AI will deploy Vera Rubin NVL72 and scale Grok on the platform, with significant scale expected in 2028. Groq 3 LPX enters full production at 3,400 tokens/sec (4x nearest competitor), with Nebius first to adopt. Separately, tens of millions in NVDA call options were sold today, and markets are not pricing in significant risk into this week's print.

bullets.title: NVDA price hikes incoming as memory costs soar; hyperscalers to bear cost
bullets.body: Nvidia is informing hyperscalers of incoming price hikes as memory costs surge significantly. One analyst noted the most obvious implication is that early Blackwell/Rubin buyers (before Jan 31, 2027) benefit from locking in prices before GPU inflation, though it's unclear whether GPU inflation outpaces rack infrastructure price growth. Amazon separately flagged 60% price increases on memory products.

bullets.title: NVDA commits $6B to open-source AI; Lancium strategic investment at 15+ GW
bullets.body: Nvidia is reportedly committing $6B to open-source initiatives as Jensen Huang pursues a full-stack strategy. Separately, NVIDIA made a strategic investment in Lancium and will deploy its full-stack AI factory platform targeting a 15+ GW portfolio. Hugging Face acquisition speculation (AWS or SpaceXAI) also circulating.

bullets.title: MU and SNDK: bulls hold but bear sentiment picks up ahead of cycle peak debate
bullets.body: A self-described AI memory/storage bull says MU and SNDK remain their largest delta-dollar positions and that both companies should be buying back stock at current levels; Hot Chips memory presentations viewed positively. However, bearish accounts are highlighting downward momentum with emoji flags, and one trader challenges whether MU and SNDK are at a cycle peak.

bullets.title: WDC in bear market: -21% last week, -43% from June peak
bullets.body: Western Digital is down 21% over the last week and making new lows in a bear market that began mid-June, with a 43% drawdown from peak. Despite the sharp decline, WDC remains up 53% over the last six months.

bullets.title: Pelosi buys up to $12M in BE (Bloom Energy) and $1.5M in INTC
bullets.body: Nancy Pelosi disclosed up to $13.5M in new stock trades: up to $12M in Bloom Energy (BE) shares and call options (expiring 06/17/2027), and up to $1.5M in Intel (INTC) with LEAP calls. Traders tie the BE position to AI data center behind-the-meter power demand, noting bipartisan political support for energy-efficient data center infrastructure.

bullets.title: ARM AGI CPU targets $2B demand in 2027-28; dual chiplets, 136 Neoverse V3 cores
bullets.body: ARM dissected its AGI CPU architecture at Hot Chips, featuring dual chiplets with over 100 billion transistors and 136 Neoverse V3 cores. The chip is expected to drive $2B in demand by 2027-2028, positioning ARM in the agentic AI silicon race alongside NVIDIA Vera.

bullets.title: Semis -3.7% on the day; sector rotation into equal-weight, defensive names
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector fell 3.7% on the session while the S&P 500 Equal Weight gained 0.2%, software fell 1%, and QQQs dropped 1.5%. One account notes repeated early-morning QQQ sell-offs that are 'like clockwork,' and highlights capital rotating from AI-heavy names into beaten-down names like TGT (up 35% since early July). NVDA is the 7th down day.

bullets.title: Trump announces 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, steel, parts effective Jan 1, 2027
bullets.body: Trump posted on Truth Social announcing 50% tariffs on all Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts, and steel effective January 1, 2027, with zero tariffs for goods built in the U.S. Canada PM Carney called the threat 'not a surprise' and said a mutually beneficial deal is still possible. Ontario Premier Doug Ford called for retaliatory cuts to U.S. electricity and critical minerals exports. VP Vance confirmed ongoing negotiations but said Ottawa made unreasonable last-minute demands.

bullets.title: US eyes 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods ahead of Sept 24 Trump-Xi meeting
bullets.body: The U.S. is considering a new 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods, which would raise total Trump second-term China tariffs to ~20%. The move is driven by excess manufacturing capacity concerns and is timed ahead of the September 24 Trump-Xi summit. White House characterized non-White House tariff news as speculation.

bullets.title: Bessent unveils 'Operation Economic Outcast': sweeping Iran sanctions, major bank to be sanctioned this week
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced a 'zero-leakage' approach to Iran sanctions, targeting five sectors for secondary sanctions: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping. Nearly 60 Iran-linked entities were sanctioned. Bessent warned every country faces defined timelines to sever Iran banking ties, and signaled a major financial institution will be sanctioned by week's end. Countries aiding Iran face exclusion from the dollar system.

bullets.title: Treasury may tap $935B TGA for bond buybacks; gold rallies to 3-month high
bullets.body: Reports suggest Treasury could deploy its ~$935B cash reserve (TGA) to fund bond buybacks rather than issue new debt, with the next buyback operation scheduled for September 9. Gold jumped to a 3-month high and the yield curve flattened on the news. Citadel Securities warned the plan risks dollar weakness and inflation. Japan's 10-year yield hit a 28-year high above 2.95%.

bullets.title: AAOI avoided LTAs to preserve capacity flexibility, required larger ATM offerings
bullets.body: Commentary notes AAOI deliberately avoided long-term customer agreements (LTAs) to maintain capacity flexibility for other customers. Without LTA prepayment financing, the company needed to execute larger at-the-market equity offerings instead.

bullets.title: IREN: trader issues short IREN / long MSTR pair trade for rest of 2026
bullets.body: One fintwit trader put out a paired trade idea: short IREN, long MSTR for the remainder of 2026, citing IREN is unlikely to catch bids near current levels despite reasonable valuation. CIFR also flagged as trading ~20% below its 200-day moving average with poor chart structure.

bullets.title: AI capex projected at $765B in 2026, surpassing oil & gas for first time
bullets.body: AI capex is forecast to reach $765B in 2026, passing oil and gas spending for the first time. Hyperscalers have lined up $2.6T in future capex commitments. Cumulative AI capex is projected near $3T by year-end, driving record debt issuance. A compute futures contract has also been launched.

bullets.title: US crude inventory at 50-year low; distillates at lowest since 1996
bullets.body: US crude oil inventory fell to 41 days of supply, the lowest in 50 years, with the SPR at 289.7M barrels (lowest since 1982) after a 3.7M barrel weekly draw. US distillate inventories hit their lowest level since 1996. Oil shipping through the Strait of Hormuz costs ~$20M per supertanker or ~$10/barrel, per TotalEnergies CEO.

bullets.title: META sees $2M+ in far OTM call buying; short-term tech call sellers also active
bullets.body: Someone purchased $2M+ of far out-of-the-money META calls, signaling bullish speculative positioning. Separately, millions in short-term tech calls were sold across the sector, and no bullish SPX orders above $500K notional were observed in one recent hour.

bullets.title: Google TPU shipments forecast to surpass NVIDIA by 2028
bullets.body: Analyst Jeff Pu expects Google TPU shipments to exceed NVIDIA's by 2028, implying a potential market share shift in AI accelerator silicon over the next two years.

bullets.title: Netflix, Peacock, Fox One distribution talks surfaced; media streaming consolidation signal
bullets.body: Executives discussed making Peacock (CMCSA) and Fox One (FOXA) available through the Netflix app, per NYT reporting. No deal announced but the conversations signal continued streaming distribution consolidation pressure.

bullets.title: SMR: Nano Nuclear Energy signs commercial data center nuclear power framework
bullets.body: Nano Nuclear Energy (SMR) signed a commercial framework agreement with Tillman to enable nuclear power supply for data centers, representing a commercialization step for small modular reactor technology targeting the AI infrastructure power demand wave.
